title: Indications, Goals & Hazards of Mechanical Ventilation Quiz

questions.text: A patient has a PaO₂ of 52 mmHg, PaCO₂ of 38 mmHg, and an elevated P(A-a)O₂ gradient. Which type of respiratory failure does this represent?

answers.text: Type I — hypoxemic respiratory failure
Type II — hypercapnic respiratory failure
Chronic respiratory failure
Impending respiratory failure only

questions.text: A patient with ARDS receives 100% FiO₂ but the PaO₂ remains critically low. What mechanism best explains this refractory hypoxemia?

answers.text: Intrapulmonary shunt — blood bypasses ventilated alveoli
V/Q mismatch — perfusion exceeds ventilation
Diffusion impairment — oxygen cannot cross the membrane
Decreased PiO₂ — inspired oxygen partial pressure is too low

questions.text: What is the normal V/Q ratio and what does a V/Q of zero indicate?

answers.text: Normal V/Q = 0.8; V/Q = 0 indicates a shunt (no ventilation)
Normal V/Q = 1.0; V/Q = 0 indicates dead space (no perfusion)
Normal V/Q = 0.8; V/Q = 0 indicates dead space (no perfusion)
Normal V/Q = 1.0; V/Q = 0 indicates a shunt (no ventilation)

questions.text: A 68-year-old patient with a COPD exacerbation has a PaCO₂ of 68 mmHg and pH of 7.22. This most likely represents:

answers.text: Type II respiratory failure due to decreased alveolar minute volume
Type I respiratory failure due to V/Q mismatch
Metabolic acidosis unrelated to ventilation
Normal compensation for chronic lung disease

questions.text: Which bedside spirometry finding most strongly indicates the need for mechanical ventilation?

answers.text: Vital capacity of 8 mL/kg with a respiratory rate of 38 breaths/min
Vital capacity of 14 mL/kg with a respiratory rate of 22 breaths/min
MIP of −30 cmH₂O with a tidal volume of 6 mL/kg
PaCO₂ of 48 mmHg with a pH of 7.34

questions.text: A patient's MIP is measured at −18 cmH₂O. How should this value be interpreted?

answers.text: Inadequate — the threshold for concern is MIP greater than −20 cmH₂O (i.e., weaker than −20)
Adequate — −18 cmH₂O is well beyond the −20 cmH₂O threshold
The MIP value is within normal limits and no action is needed
MIP is not a reliable parameter for determining need for mechanical ventilation

questions.text: Which physiologic measurement indicates increased work of breathing and suggests the need for ventilatory support?

answers.text: Minute volume > 10 L/min and VD/Vt > 0.60
PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio > 300 and P(A-a)O₂ < 100
PaCO₂ < 35 mmHg and pH > 7.45
Spontaneous tidal volume > 8 mL/kg and RR of 14

questions.text: Which of the following is a CONTRAINDICATION to initiating mechanical ventilation?

answers.text: Patient has a valid DNI order and does not wish to be intubated
PaO₂ of 52 mmHg on high-flow oxygen
pH of 7.18 with PaCO₂ of 62 mmHg
Respiratory rate of 38 breaths/min with a Vt of 4 mL/kg

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes a GOAL of mechanical ventilation?

answers.text: Reduce the work of breathing and restore acid-base balance
Eliminate the need for sedation and analgesia
Increase venous return to improve cardiac output
Prevent alveolar recruitment to reduce barotrauma

questions.text: A mechanically ventilated ICU patient develops worsening oxygenation, decreased blood pressure, and decreased urine output. Which hazards of mechanical ventilation best explain these findings?

answers.text: Oxygen toxicity, decreased venous return, and decreased urinary output from reduced cardiac output
Auto-PEEP, nosocomial pneumonia, and ventilator-induced lung injury
Barotrauma, atelectasis, and lack of nutrition
Increased intracranial pressure, VILI, and decreased urinary output
